summary: Package opens WebSocket to hardcoded relay that drives host input and permission-skipped Claude Code
details: cli.js connects to a hardcoded WebSocket relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and treats incoming messages as commands: type/click/key/scroll messages are converted into real keyboard and mouse events on the host via @nut-tree-fork/nut-js, and ai_query/ai_voice_query messages spawn the local `claude` CLI with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` using prompt text supplied by the remote peer. Whoever controls the relay (or any party able to connect to it as the peer) can drive arbitrary input into the installer's desktop session and invoke an AI coding agent with all permission prompts bypassed, giving remote code and file-system access on the host. A secondary handler (transcribeOgg) also fetches an arbitrary URL supplied by the relay in ai_voice_query.fileUrl and writes it to /tmp before passing it to ffmpeg/whisper, letting the remote peer drive outbound HTTP requests from the host. Although the package's documented purpose is remote control of Claude Code, the trust anchor is a single hardcoded third-party relay under the maintainer's control rather than an installer-configured endpoint, and the ai_* path unconditionally passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
